Items available 8am-6pm:
**Keoghtom’s Ointment** Wondrous item 750g
This glass jar, 3 inches in diameter, contains 1d4 + 1 doses of a thick mixture that smells faintly of aloe. The jar and its contents weigh 1/2 pound. As an action, one dose of the ointment can be swallowed or applied to the skin. The creature that receives it regains 2d8 + 2 hit points, ceases to be poisoned, and is cured of any disease.

**Gaillardia’s Healing Salve** 1,300g
This jar contains a greasy, yellow, jellylike substance. A single application of healing salve smeared across a wound heals 1d8+1 points of damage. A double application heals 2d8+3 points of damage. A triple application heals 3d8+5 points of damage. No matter how much salve is used, each application takes a standard action to apply. A 3-inch-diameter, 2-inch-deep jar holds enough salve for ten single applications.

**Potion of Regular Healing** 200g

**24 Hour Potion of Greater Healing**- Limit 1 per day, 1st come, first served. 400g
Regular potion of greater healing with an expiration of 24 hours.

**Oil of Etherealness **, rare 2,000g
Beads of this cloudy gray oil form on the outside of its container and quickly evaporate. The oil can cover a Medium or smaller creature, along with the equipment it’s wearing and carrying (one additional vial is required for each size category above Medium). Applying the oil takes 10 minutes. The affected creature then gains the effect of the etherealness spell for 1 hour.

**Oil of Sharpness **, very rare 5,000g
This clear, gelatinous oil sparkles with tiny, ultrathin silver shards. The oil can coat one slashing or piercing weapon or up to 5 pieces of slashing or piercing ammunition. Applying the oil takes 1 minute. For 1 hour, the coated item is magical and has a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls.

**Oil of Slipperiness**, uncommon 500g
This sticky black unguent is thick and heavy in the container, but it flows quickly when poured. The oil can cover a Medium or smaller creature, along with the equipment it’s wearing and carrying (one additional vial is required for each size category above Medium). Applying the oil takes 10 minutes. The affected creature then gains the effect of a freedom of movement spell for 8 hours.
Alternatively, the oil can be poured on the ground as an action, where it covers a 10-foot square, duplicating the effect of the grease spell in that area for 8 hours.

**Potion of Invisibility**, very rare 200g
This potion’s container looks empty but feels as though it holds liquid. When you drink it, you become invisible for 1 hour. Anything you wear or carry is invisible with you. The effect ends early if you attack or cast a spell.

**Potion of Heroism** , rare 200g
For 1 hour after drinking it, you gain 10 temporary hit points that last for 1 hour. For the same duration, you are under the effect of the bless spell (no concentration required). This blue potion bubbles and steams as if boiling.

**DAYTIME ITEMS AVAILABLE:
**
**Penney’s Peerless Power Polishes**-Wondrous item (consumable) 800g
A brand of black market nail polish often used to smuggle magic into places where it aught not belong. Mixed with a dash of powdered lead to block magic detection from spells and abilities that would do so. You can only cast these spells once per application and only one color may be applied at a time. Each bottle has 5 applications.Currently on the market there are only six colors each with their own effect:

      *Revolutionary Red*: Your fierce passion for the cause explodes out with this polish. You can cast  Fireball(3rd level, DC 14).
      *Ben’s Brilliant Blue*: Be as smart, striking, and fashionable as the big brain himself, Benjamin Franklin. Strike a pose and you can cast Lightning 
           Bolt(3rd level, DC14).
     *Proletarian Pink*: Penney’s personal polish, practical, pure, and a protector of proletarian. Stand before you fellows and lead them to rise up. You can  cast Motivational Speech(3rd level).

**Ka-zoom** Bardic instrument (requires attunement by a bard) 2,000g
This magical kazoo add +1 to your Spell Attack bonus and spell save DC while attuned to it.
As a bonus action you can blow into the Ka-zoom to cast Haste on yourself. The effect persists for a number of rounds equal to your Con modifier (minimum of 1)

**Lyre's Chord** Bardic instrument (requires attunement by a bard) 2,000
Carved from Fae'd Oak and strung with Strands of Ley, any who hear the melodies plucked have their confidence in themselves bolstered. Whenever someone uses your bardic inspiration they can roll the die twice and take the higher of the two.

**Crown of Cael'fii Rare**, Wondrous item (requires attunement by spellcaster) 4,500g 
A crown woven from twigs pulled from the branches of Cael'fii. Once attuned to the crown you can now cast the Shillelagh cantrip, if you don’t already know it. While attuned the cantrip is modified in the following ways: -you may use this cantrip on any weapon made of wood. -as an action, you may make a special attack that releases the magical powers imbued into the weapon. Make a melee spell attack against the target. On a hit, the weapon deals an extra 1d8 damage (2d8) and the spell ends.

**Gauntlet of the Seasons Wondrous Item** (requires attunement) 4,000g
This gauntlet appears to be carved from white oak. A pink Opal, red Jasper, orange Carnelian, and Lapis Lazuli are inlaid across the top of knuckles. Unarmed Strikes get +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls. These gauntlets have 5 charges, which are refreshed at dawn each morning. As a part of an attack action you may spend a charge to add the power of one of the seasons to your attack. The target takes an additional 2d4 damage. Choose one of the d4s. The number rolled on that die determines the additional damage type, as shown below. d4 | Damage Type 1 | Radiant 2 | Fire 3 | Necromantic 4 | Cold If you roll the same number on both d4s, the power of the season leaps from the target to a different creature of your choice within 10 feet of it. Make an attack roll against the new target, and roll a new 2d4 damage roll, which could cause the power of the seasons to leap again. A creature can be targeted only once by each use of the gauntlet.

**Prosthetic Limb** Wondrous item, common 100g
This item replaces a lost limb a hand, an arm, a foot, a leg, or a similar body part. While the prosthetic is attached, it functions identically to the part it replaces. You can detach or reattach it as an action, and it can't be removed against your will. It detaches if you die. Limbs grown from this shop apear as branches  on their hosts.

**Dr. Wynn’s Herbalist Bag **Wondrous item 1,000g
A leather bag, made from different animal hides and stitched together with plant fibers, the interior has numerous pockets, each with an embroidered plant on the side. This bag counts as an herbalist’s kit and gives the wielder advantage on checks to find and identify herbs. This bag also contains 10 charges, using the herbs you may spend up to three charges as a bonus action to heal someone 1d6 hit points per charge. The charges refresh if you spend at least an hour searching for herbs or spend at least 50gp on resupplying the bag.

**NIGHTTIME ITEMS AVAILABLE:**

**Penney’s Peerless Power Polishes**-Wondrous item (consumable) 600g
A brand of black market nail polish often used to smuggle magic into places where it aught not belong. Mixed with a dash of powdered lead to block magic detection from spells and abilities that would do so. You can only cast these spells once per application and only one color may be applied at a time. Each bottle has 5 applications.Currently on the market there are only six colors each with their own effect:

     *Cat’s Paw Purple:* Display how safe and innocent you are with a simple flourish of your hand, before striking your foe. You can cast Hypnotic 
          Pattern(3rd level, DC14).
     *Bear-garden Black:* Interrupt those that would try to cast down on you with a raucous interjection. You can cast Counterspell(3rd level, only affects 
          spells of 3rd level or lower).
     *Gillygaupus Green*: Some consider this green to be a bit silly, prove them wrong and show them they are true Gillyguapus. You can cast Bestow 
            Curse(3rd level, DC14, no concentration).

**Wilhelm’s Folly Rare**, quarterstaff (requires attunement) 2,000g
Requires at least 16 Charisma
A staff designed for a mad comic who wished to “...really blow the audience away.” Atop the head of the staff is an enchanted metal cage that amplifies it’s users voice three fold. This staff has 7 charges. While attuned to it you may use the charges in the following ways.
 Spend 3 charges to cast a 3rd level Pulse Wave spell (push only, save DC 15)
Spend 2 charges for the staff to act as a 3rd level Spiritual Weapon spell. When being used in this way you can’t use the staff for anything else until the spell ends.
Spend 3 charges to cast Hideous Laughter spell (save DC 15) on up to 3 targets within 30ft of each other.
This staff regains 1d6+1 charges daily at dawn.

**Mask of the Unassuming** Wondrous item (requires attunement by a spellcaster) 3,000g
A half mask that covers the lower half of the wearer’s face. It can appear to be the lower half of a face or simple face covering. While wearing this mask and attuned to it, you can ignore the vocal component of any spells you cast and Counterspells have disadvantage against your spells. You also have a +5 on Dexterity(Stealth) and Charisma(Deception) checks when trying to blend in with a crowd.

**Moon Thistle Bonsai** (Requires attunement by a druid or ranger) 250g
A small potted tree that's branches can be harvested daily to make 1d6 magical wooden ammunition for a Bow or Crossbow. It regrows every night as long as it bathes in moonlight. You can trim up to 1d6 wooden magical ammo that lasts up to 24 hours before losing their potency.

**Darling's Duster** Wondrous Item (requires attunement) 1,500g
A maroon duster with mustard yellow silk lining covered in a paisley pattern of teal and aqua. The coat has four large pockets on the interior of the coat, each is large enough for a standard book. Stitched into one of the pockets is the word "Bookworm." As the coattails flow near the floor wisps of smoke or mist (your choice) pour from beneath. While you are attuned to this item you can cast Fog Cloud at will, (1st level version, centered on yourself). Once per day you may cast gaseous form on yourself, this ability recharges at dawn.

**Feywild Shard** Wondrous item uncommon (requires attunement by a sorcerer) 750g
This warm crystal glints with the sunset colors of the Feywild sky and evokes whispers of emotional memory. As an action, you can attach the shard to a Tiny object (such as a weapon or a piece of jewelry) or detach it. It falls off if your attunement to it ends. You can use the shard as a spellcasting focus while you hold or wear it.
When you use a Metamagic option on a spell while you are holding or wearing the shard, you can roll on the Wild Magic Surge table in the Player's Handbook. If the result is a spell, it is too wild to be affected by your Metamagic, and if it normally requires concentration, it doesn't require concentration in this case; the spell lasts for its full duration.
If you don't have the Wild Magic Sorcerous Origin, once this property is used to roll on the Wild Magic Surge table, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

**Twig of Power**, Staff or Wand depending on size 5,000g (requires attunement)
For medium or larger creatures it is treated as a wand and for creatures size small or smaller this item is treated as a quarterstaff that grants a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. While holding it, you gain a +1 to Armor Class, +1 to spell attack rolls, and your spell save DC.
The Twig has 10 charges for the following properties. The staff regains 1d8+2 charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the Twig loses all properties and crumbles to dust. On a 20, the Twig regains 1d4+1 charges.

*Power Strike*. When a small creature hits with a melee attack using the Twig, you can expend a charge to deal 1d4 force damage to the target.

*Magic Dart*. As a staff or wand you can expend a charge to shoot a sliver of magic at a target for 3 force damage. (works similar to Magic Missile)

*Spells*. While wielding this staff or wand, you can use an action to expend 1 or more of it’s charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC and spell attack bonus: Snowball Swarm (2 charges), Chromatic Orb (2nd level version, fire damage, 2 charges), Shield of Faith (No concentration, 3 charges), Hold Person (2 charges), Levitate (1 charges), Lightning Bolt (3 charges), Ray of Enfeeblement (1 charge), Shield (1 charge)

*Retributive Strike.* You can use an action to break the Twig over your knee or against a solid surface, performing a retributive strike. The Twig is destroyed and releases its remaining magic, an explosion that expands to fill a 20 foot radius sphere centered on it.
You have a 50 percent chance to instantly travel to a random plane of existence, avoiding the explosion. If you fail to avoid the effect, you take force damage equal to 8 * the number of charges in the staff. Every other creature in the area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes an amount of damage based on how far away it is from the point of origin, as shown below. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage.

Distance from Origin        Effect
Less than 10ft away         4 * the number of charges
10 to 15ft away                  3 * the number of charges
16 to 20ft away                 2 * the number of charges

A large market district in the center of Ferrytown that borders on and overlaps with several natural areas. If you want strange curios and other oddities, this is where you go. The shops are run by Seelie fey during the day and Unseelie fey during the night, meaning that different products may be available at different times.

Illo’fae is a large fairground at the South of burrough. Entirely fairground/amusement park, including park areas. This is the perfect place to spend a sunny day off enjoying various games, shows, and delicacies. It is also home to a luxury hotel structured entirely of the surrounding trees.

Stretching taller than most other buildings in Ferrytown, this area between the Sunrise and Sunset ports is home to visitors accustomed to more built-up dwellings. It also houses a population of mostly elf traders who commute to The City from Ferrytown each day.

Named for the original human residents, Jameco is a community built primarily of these native peoples and fey bleed over. It is home to the Ferrytown court and resides between The Mounds and Grassy Bay. The sacred tree, Cael'fii, grows here.
Near the north end of Ferrytown and in full view of The City, the Sunrise Port is the main ferry port transporting between Ferrytown and The City, as well as up the channels to Kingsbridge.
West of The Hilltops, the Sunset Port is the main ferry port transporting across the river from the Empire City.

A stretch of hilly terrain near the center of Ferrytown, the East and West Hills are both places of feywild bleed over, though they are not connected. The most 'outsider friendly' of the feywild parks, they are adjacent to The Bustle and often full of younger teens and children, staying pleasantly warm for most of the day and year.

Situated on the south corner of the Western Hilltop park, this pub made of stone and wood is split down the middle and has two entrances: one on the feywild bleed side, and one that leads out into the more mundane section of The Bustle. There are no rules or firm divisions between the two sides, and mingling occurs frequently. No to-go orders are allowed. All drinks must be consumed on the premises. The interior of the bar appears more slanted and uneven the more you approach the fey side, making it difficult not to spill your drink.

This stall is run by a large bugbear man who talks in extremely dramatic fashion. Many of his pieces of armor are fancy and catching to the eye. He ages his whole lifespan over the course of a day, his taste and required gifts changing with him. The interior of the stall, which is an open-air blacksmithy with a small room in the back for sleeping, has several clocks strewn about. As the day progresses, the bugbear man will go by different variants of the same name: JJ, Jimmy, John, James, and Johnathan. Information on the items sold here can be found in the ferrytown burrough channel. Unlike many of the other shops in Ferrytown which take on a different tone and goods during the night, this shop is instead closed as the bugbear begins to die at sunset and is reborn and ages enough to manage the shop by sunrise.

All items are made of Fae'd Oak- Weapons or Armor made from this wyld wood have no metal within them, but are just as sturdy as their metal counterparts. Armor made from this Fae'd Oak gives resistance to Psychic and Force Damage. Weapons carved from Fae'd Oak are much less common, mainly because of their instability, when you Crit with these weapons roll on the Fae'd Oak wild magic table:

1- Sap pours from the palm of your hands and hardens around whatever weapon you are wielding. For the next 10 minutes the weapon deals an extra damage die of force damage on the first attack that hits and you cannot be disarmed and not use whatever hand or hands are stuck to the weapon.
2- The latent Fae magic in the weapon surges from within it and into you, revitalizing your stamina. You can roll a d6+2 or a d8+2 and gain that number of hit points or temporary hit points, respectively.
3- A flumph appears in an empty location of your choosing within 30 feet of you. It, startled at both the sudden atomization and deatomization, uses its Stench Spray ability and disappears at the start of your next turn.
4- Large vines and roots grow out of the weapon, wrapping around you, and planting themselves into the ground surrounding you. For the next minute or until you take 20 damage the ground 10 feet within you becomes difficult terrain, you gain +2 AC, and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
5- You strike with impeccable flourish, alluring nearby enemies. Up to 3 hostile creatures within 30 feet of you must succeed on a wisdom saving throw, DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your charisma modifier, or become charmed for 10 minutes.
6- The wrath of the seasons lash out from the weapon. All enemies within 15 feet of you take 1d6 fire damage, 1d6 cold damage, are pushed back 5 feet, and have their speed reduced to zero until your next turn.
7- The strong force of your strike summons a benevolent nature spirit. The spirit has the statistics of an Awakened Tree, except it is a small fae instead of a huge plant. It takes its turn immediately after yours and can be commanded (no action required). It remains for 10 minutes before returning to the feywild.
8- The frigid clutch of the Unseelie court blesses you. Armor of Agathys is cast on you at second level, and lasts for the next 10 minutes.

How I thought I'll do it for the initial infodump so you have something to check without having to wait for me is have messages that are kinda section separators and pin those so it'll be quicker to scroll through in the dropdown menu with pins, and then you can click them and go to the full text.

Most of the command info is in `?help` output (`?help command-name` for specific ones, as expected).
Commands for DMs are a bit more complex than the general ones, so while for the general commands you can get by with just `?help`, for DM commands `?help` won't contain everything for usability, and here will have more stuff like examples, and also stuff about the bot's automatic functions.
If something will need editing I'll edit it, otherwise I'll pin answers to any questions that might pop up
↓ What the bot does automatically ↓

- **scheduled messages**: main thing. The bot keeps messages to be sent once daily or once ever at specified times, to the specific channel.
- **clock**: at specified times (6 am, noon, 6 pm, 9 pm) there'll be a message in <#851552515345350657>, and messages older than 24h are deleted.
- **stocks**: every day at 6 am the bot will read new stock prices from Rob's spreadsheet
- **PC location tracking**: every time someone makes a message (except for OOC or any hidden channels), unless they're skipped from tracking (DMs and bots are), the bot takes note of the channel, so later anyone can check where someone was last. If someone was inactive for 24h they're removed from the list.
- **reactions**: if someone makes a message in a tracked channel, and it contains a specific word, the bot will add an emoji reaction to it
- **pins**: every time a message is pinned, that little "someone pinned a message to this channel" notification will be removed after 10 minutes
- **rollover**: every midnight the bot reloads its stuff, so errors don't accumulate. This does not take the bot offline.
- **automatic uptime**: if something in the code shits the bed and the bot goes down, it'll come back online within 5 minutes
↓ tl;dr of the commands all server members can use ↓

`?help`: displays command list with a tl;dr for each, `?help command-name` gives details for that command. Only commands you can use are visible and usable.

`?stocks`: lets players deal with stocks as set up by Rob, on its own the command lists prices, `?stocks mine` shows the player's portfolio, `?stocks buy` and `?stocks sell` do what they sound like

`?time`: displays current server time

`?where` shows which IC channel someone was last active, you can give it an @-mention, or a full display name, or the beginning of the display name (`?where roy` should match me now)

All commands are usable by private message to the bot, or in any channel in the server, but not in any other server.
↓ commands for DMs ↓

`?reaction` - adds an emoji reaction for the bot to use.
Called like `?reaction :fire_extinguisher: fireball`
will make it so if someone says "fireball" in an IC channel, the bot will add 🧯 as a reaction to the message

`?tasks`: shows if the automated tasks (not the act-on-a-message ones) are running right. It's ok if it says "running" for all of them, or "stopped" for "messages" task - that just means it ran out of messages for the day and will resume at midnight
`?stocks reload`: manually reload stock prices from Rob's spreadsheet. Normally shouldn't be needed, but just in case

`?message`: this is a big one. This command gives easier access to adding new scheduled messages to the bot, and is an extension of the file format I set up for holding those messages. The only thing about that format you need to worry about is how mentions are represented there, which is usable here too, which I'll describe in a bit.

Before I write any details, note that **this command has an interactive variant:** `?message interactive` (or just `?message i`), **which guides you through the process step-by-step**.
The only things you need to know for it is 1) that you can add a timeout in seconds (like `?message i 60` for 60 seconds) and that's how long the bot will wait for your response, default is 30. 2) how the plaintext mentions work if you don't want to ping people when setting the message up. If you plan to only use interactive, you can skip the rest of this message, and if you don't plan to use plaintext mentions, you can skip that one too.

To submit a message through the command, you call the command like this:
```
?message 2021-08-01 14:00 #new-player-landing
hello this is the start of the message content
all the stuff till the end of the message counts as text for the new message to schedule
that includes all the mentions that might be here, both normal ones and the plaintext ones
```
- timestamp: is `HH:MM` for daily messages, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` for one-time messages. Server time, 24h clock.
- channel: either channel name, or the clickable #-link to it
- message: obviously must be under character limit, but the header line will ensure that. Can have the normal, clickable, ping-making mentions, and can contain the plaintext mention placeholders as mentioned above, details about them in the next message.
↓ how the square brackets plaintext mentions work (completely optional) ↓

They look like this: `@[some stuff in square brackets]` and don't make the clickable pinging mentions, but let you do a fuzzy match.
That was needed for adding messages directly to files on Dropbox, but isn't required here. The biggest use cases are doing @[everyone] or if you don't want to ping fellow DMs while setting up the message.
Other than that, people *should not* get pinged by mentions in channels they can't access. At least our recent tests show that.

The way that works is by trying to match the stuff in square brackets to something - the first thing from this list is what gets used:
- if it's `@[everyone]`, it'll be converted into an everyone ping when the scheduled message is sent.
- role by role name
- player by their discord id (the long one)
- player by exact current displayed name, if they've been active in the last 24h
- player by their nickname otherwise, or by their account name, or account name with 4-digit discriminator (like Versil#6074), but not nickname + discriminator
- player by beginning part of their displayed name or account name, ignoring case (so for example @[ver] would match Versil)

So in a practical example:
- account name: `Versil`
- account discriminator: `6074`
- server nickname: `Roy | Versil (H)`
- account id: `148682928434577408`

All the following will work:
- account name, `@[Versil]`
- part of account name, even lowercase, `@[vers]`
- server nickname, `@[Roy | Versil (H)]`
- part of server nickname, even lowercase, `@[roy | versil]` or `@[roy]`
- account name + discriminator, `@[Versil#6074]`
- account id, `@[148682928434577408]`

This one **will definitely not work** (but is pointless as you shouldn't need the discriminator):
- server nickname + discriminator, `@[Roy | Versil (H)#6074]`

It might happen that the input can match multiple people - you might not get the right result then, and I can't guarantee it'd get the person you want - it won't do multiple at once.
